I have to stop here rather than hand you a tarball, because partway through I found something that changes what this session can safely produce.

The dump is one slice behind your working tree
dump.txt was generated at commit 7172839 (2026-08-01 21:49 EDT). That is M6 Slice 5. Your build output is from after Slice 6 — the slice that added scenarios 4 and 6, plus the CS1620 fix. I confirmed this three ways:

The dump's EndToEndScenarios.cs is 559 lines; your errors cite lines 566 and 568.
The dump's TableJourneys.cs:113 still contains the string.Create call that produced CS1620 — the bug you've since fixed.
github.com/kusl/myrestaurant@main is also still at that state. EndToEndScenarios.cs is 31,473 bytes there (byte-identical to the dump), there is no Harness/TableOrderJourneys.cs or Harness/KitchenJourneys.cs, and no docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-m6-slice-6.md. Slice 6 exists only on your disk.
So I can't give you a correct full EndToEndScenarios.cs, and I can't write scenario 5 — it needs TableOrderJourneys, KitchenJourneys, the GuestOrderLine/GuestLineBadge vocabulary and RestaurantInstance.VerifyInteractivityAsync, none of which I can see. Guessing at a full file that overwrites Slice 6's work is the one failure mode your delivery format is designed to prevent, so I won't.

Please re-run bash export.sh and upload the fresh dump. Then scenario 5 and the E2E fixes go in the next archive.

What I did verify and can hand you now
The xUnit2031 fix is mechanical. Rewrite Assert.Single(xs.Where(p)) → Assert.Single(xs, p). I confirmed against xunit/assert.xunit that the overload is public static T Single<T>(IEnumerable<T> collection, Predicate<T> predicate) — it returns T, so assignments still bind. Two of your four sites I recovered verbatim (scenario 6, the ones at columns 35 and 34):

csharp
GuestOrderLine soupLine = Assert.Single(
    afterFulfillment, line => line.Name.Contains(service.Soup.Name, StringComparison.Ordinal));
GuestOrderLine pieLine = Assert.Single(
    afterFulfillment, line => line.Name.Contains(service.Pie.Name, StringComparison.Ordinal));
The two at 477/479 (column 13) follow the same shape. Worth doing rather than suppressing: the predicate overload reports the whole collection on failure, where .Where(…) reports only the empty filtered result — which is exactly the diagnostic you want from an E2E failure.

The package bump is safe, and I've written it. Net.Codecrete.QrCodeGenerator 3.0.0 → 3.1.0 is purely additive — the release note is balanced sizing for structured append, which nothing here uses. I checked the v3.1.0 tag directly: EncodeText(string, Ecc), Size, and ToGraphicsPath(int border = 0) all carry identical signatures, and no test pins a golden module path. One caveat worth naming: central package management moves the web app and the E2E project together, which is what keeps JoinQrCodes' recomputed-path assertion meaningful.

Nothing else is outdated. dotnet list package --outdated can't see NSubstitute because no project references it — I checked by hand, and 6.0.0 is current.

Docs are safe to edit and genuinely stale. Slice 6 touched 9 files, none of them documentation, so these don't collide. README still says "five of the fifteen" (it's eight: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 13, 14, 15) and "~934 facts" (971 total / 956 succeeded / 15 skipped). I'd also add a ledger row — the guest-registration gap from Slice 5 never got one, despite the atomic-documentation rule, and the unrated-limited /register belongs in §17's accepted risks.

Send the fresh dump and I'll ship all of it in one archive.

What I did verify and can hand you now
The xUnit2031 fix is mechanical. Rewrite Assert.Single(xs.Where(p)) → Assert.Single(xs, p). I confirmed against xunit/assert.xunit that the overload is public static T Single<T>(IEnumerable<T> collection, Predicate<T> predicate) — it returns T, so assignments still bind. Two of your four sites I recovered verbatim (scenario 6, the ones at columns 35 and 34):

csharp
GuestOrderLine soupLine = Assert.Single(
    afterFulfillment, line => line.Name.Contains(service.Soup.Name, StringComparison.Ordinal));
GuestOrderLine pieLine = Assert.Single(
    afterFulfillment, line => line.Name.Contains(service.Pie.Name, StringComparison.Ordinal));
The two at 477/479 (column 13) follow the same shape. Worth doing rather than suppressing: the predicate overload reports the whole collection on failure, where .Where(…) reports only the empty filtered result — which is exactly the diagnostic you want from an E2E failure.

The package bump is safe, and I've written it. Net.Codecrete.QrCodeGenerator 3.0.0 → 3.1.0 is purely additive — the release note is balanced sizing for structured append, which nothing here uses. I checked the v3.1.0 tag directly: EncodeText(string, Ecc), Size, and ToGraphicsPath(int border = 0) all carry identical signatures, and no test pins a golden module path. One caveat worth naming: central package management moves the web app and the E2E project together, which is what keeps JoinQrCodes' recomputed-path assertion meaningful.

Nothing else is outdated. dotnet list package --outdated can't see NSubstitute because no project references it — I checked by hand, and 6.0.0 is current.

Docs are safe to edit and genuinely stale. Slice 6 touched 9 files, none of them documentation, so these don't collide. README still says "five of the fifteen" (it's eight: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 13, 14, 15) and "~934 facts" (971 total / 956 succeeded / 15 skipped). I'd also add a ledger row — the guest-registration gap from Slice 5 never got one, despite the atomic-documentation rule, and the unrated-limited /register belongs in §17's accepted risks.

M6 Slice 7 — documentation catches up, one dependency moves. 9 files, extracts at the repo root, no deletions. Not one .cs or .razor.

Nothing under tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/ is in the archive, and neither are TableOrderSurface.razor or KitchenBoard.razor — Slice 6 edited those and my snapshot predates it, so a "full file" for any of them would silently revert two scenarios.

The xUnit2031 fix ships as a parser, not a guess — docs/llm/vendor/fix_assert_single.py, in the vendor folder export.sh already excludes:

bash
python3 docs/llm/vendor/fix_assert_single.py \
  tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/EndToEndScenarios.cs --dry-run --expect 4
It rewrites only a call whose entire argument is <receiver>.Where(<lambda>), skipping every literal form and both comment forms — a ) inside "with a )() note" can't close a call early. Run across all 309 files of the Slice 5 tree it produced byte-identical output; running it twice changes nothing.

The package bump is verified, not assumed. 3.0.0 → 3.1.0 is entirely structured-append work, which nothing here uses. I read the v3.1.0 tag: EncodeText(string, Ecc), Size, ToGraphicsPath(int border = 0) unchanged. Worth knowing that CPM moves the app and the E2E project together — that's load-bearing, since JoinQrCodes recomputes the expected path with the same library, and a skew would turn scenario 2 into a test of the dependency. NSubstitute is invisible to outdated mode because nothing references it; checked by hand, 6.0.0 is current.

One bug I caught in my own work: the first draft of the props comment contained --outdated, and an XML comment may not contain two consecutive hyphens. MSBuild would have rejected the file outright. It's rephrased, and the file now parses.

The documentation finding is the substantive part. Slice 5 shipped /register and argued no spec edit was needed — correct on the narrow question, but a new anonymous route that writes a person row is a behaviour change, and the atomic-documentation rule wants a ledger row regardless. F-37 is entered now, late, and says so. It's the same shape as F-35: a requirement stated plainly, a mechanism described, and no line in §19 claiming it — so every milestone review passed, because every milestone did what its own list said. Twice is a pattern, and the ledger's closing note now names the guard. Spec goes to v1.1 with §11.8, the §17 accepted risk (including why the rate limit isn't a two-line addition), and a changelog. §11.7 keeps its number — a dozen source files cite it.
